candidates.title: OS command injection in Ping via unsanitized 'host' query parameter
candidates.rationale: The 'host' query parameter is read straight from the request and concatenated into a string passed to `sh -c`. Shell metacharacters (;, |, $(), backticks) in the value let an unauthenticated attacker run arbitrary commands as the server process.

candidates.title: Path traversal in ReadDoc via 'file' query parameter
candidates.rationale: The 'file' query parameter is appended to the '/data/' prefix with no cleaning or containment check, so values such as '../../etc/passwd' escape the intended directory and read arbitrary files readable by the process.

candidates.title: SQL injection in FindUser via string-concatenated 'id' parameter
candidates.rationale: The 'id' query parameter is concatenated into the SQL text inside single quotes and passed to db.Query, allowing classic injection such as `' OR '1'='1` to alter the query, bypass filtering, and exfiltrate rows from the users table.
candidates.evidence:
id := r.URL.Query().Get("id")
return db.Query("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = '" + id + "'")

candidates.title: Server-side request forgery in Proxy via 'url' query parameter
candidates.rationale: The 'url' query parameter is passed directly to http.Get with no scheme, host or IP allow-listing, letting an attacker make the server issue requests to internal services, loopback, or cloud metadata endpoints and relay the response back.
